findings.F1: In the rising calm profile (the bars the regime did not send to "chop"), wide days closing in the lower half of their range (range of at least 2 usual moves, close location of at least 0.5) were followed by a larger move the longer the horizon. The coin's excess return was +1.44 % over 1 day (t 2.53, 161 cases, 85 days), +2.25 % over 2 days (t 2.19, 90 cases, 47 days) and +4.14 % over 3 days (t 2.46, 64 non-overlapping cases, 32 days). The 3-day move is about 19 times the 0.22 % cost of a trade.
findings.F2: At the 3-day horizon in rising calm, across days at least 1.5 usual moves wide, the move grows with the day's width more than with where it closed. The slope of the 3-day excess return on range was +1.28 % per usual move (t 1.98, 248 cases), against +3.93 % per unit of close location (t 1.54). This is the brief's own "the wider the day, the larger the rise", which the tested idea (graded on close location only, 1 day) did not test.
findings.F3: The 3-day rebound after rising-calm wide low-close days was positive in every window with cases: w8 +3.4 %, w10 +3.1 %, w11 +2.5 %, w12 +2.7 %, w15 +0.8 %, w17 +13.6 %, w18 +7.8 %. Each window has few cases (4 to 10).
findings.F4: In rising calm, wide days closing in the upper half also rose over the next 3 days (+2.06 %, t 1.39, 79 cases) against +4.14 % for low closes. Over 1 day the 2–3 usual-move high-close days showed +0.59 % (t 1.21). In this profile a wide day leans to a rise whichever way it closed, and the low close adds to it.
findings.F5: Outside rising calm, on wide days (at least 2 usual moves) the next-day excess return rises with the close's nearness to the low: slope +2.86 % per unit of close location, t 2.92, 1241 cases. It is strongest on days of 3 or more usual moves: high closes −1.53 % (t −2.38), low closes +1.65 % (t 2.13). It is also strong in falling markets: high closes −1.31 % (t −2.05), low closes +1.15 % (t 1.69). This is the reversal family the map already holds (058-02.b1.g1.b1.b1 falling agitated next-day reversal, 060-01.g1.d2.d1 own range close height fade).
findings.F6: In rising calm, any down day was followed by a next-day rise: +0.63 % on non-wide down days (t 2.40, 479 cases, 243 days) and +1.19 % on wide ones (t 2.03). The grading by the size of the fall is only borderline: slope −0.77 % per usual move, t −1.91. Much of it comes from 2020 (+1.45 %, t 4.40), against 2018 +0.06 % and 2019 +0.23 %. The windows disagree (w12 −0.10 %, w15 −1.16 %). This is a long fall-rebound the map holds many of.
findings.F7: Rising-calm Thursdays were followed by +1.41 % (t 2.84, 271 cases). After about 80 cells were examined, this does not stand out from chance, and it repeats the held 045-01 "rising market late week gain".
findings.F8: The book's 10 best days sum to +29.5 % and its 10 worst to −18.3 %, out of a +37.5 % summed total over 1449 days. Its gain rests on a few large rebounds, consistent with its failed Calmar (0.49).

ideas.idea: In a rising, calm market, a day whose high-to-low range is wide against the coin's 30-day swing of daily returns and that closes in the lower part of its range is followed by a rise over the next three days; the wider the day against that swing, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: In an orderly uptrend, a wide low-close day is a reason to buy for a few days rather than one, sized by how wide the day was against the coin's usual swing.
ideas.name: wide low close three-day rebound

ideas.idea: In a rising, calm market, a day whose high-to-low range is wide against the coin's 30-day swing of daily returns is followed by a rise over the next three days, whichever way it closed; the wider the day against that swing, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: In an orderly uptrend, an unusually wide day is a reason to lean long for a few days, more so the wider it was, rather than to read it as the trend breaking.
ideas.name: rising calm wide day continuation
